transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help you with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing light gardening, like watering plants or gentle weeding, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid bending or heavy lifting for a month. Just remember to wear protective eyewear, like sunglasses, when you're outside. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you for the info! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using the preservative-free eye drops I recommended about 4 times a day, starting right away. You can get more drops from your GP if you need them. If you were using drops before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's helpful. I'm also very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to be sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially in the first few weeks. If it's mild, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're going outside.
